# Episode 003 approved introduction (verbatim, do not edit)

Preserved exactly as approved on 2026-10-08. SCRIPT.md uses this text unchanged in sections 01 and 02.

---

A friend of mine recently gave me two long boxes full of comic books.

Hundreds of comics he'd been collecting since he was a kid in the '90s.

And I was pretty excited, because I was about to find out two things.

First, what the hell was in these boxes?

And second, how well could the comic-book website I'd been building actually handle a real collection?

But before I get into that, I should probably explain why I started building ComixCatalog in the first place.

A few years ago, during COVID, I was living with a roommate who was constantly buying records on Discogs.

I was familiar with the website, but once he actually showed me how he used it, I started getting a little obsessed with the idea.

He could catalog his records, find specific pressings, track approximate values, and buy from sellers all over the world. He could hunt for deals without having to guess what everything was worth.

And I remember thinking about my own comic collection.

Specifically, my Coheed and Cambria comics.

I had books I wanted to find, runs I wanted to finish, and gaps in my collection. Why couldn't I just open a website, find the exact comic I needed, compare listings, and buy it?

I was just starting my master's degree in software engineering, and somewhere in there, the idea started taking shape.

What if somebody made Discogs for comics?

And what if that somebody was me?

Fast-forward to my friend Corey handing me two enormous boxes of comics.

Suddenly I had a pretty good way to find out whether the thing I'd been building actually worked.
